headline: High: ms-swift can write and egress by default, creating leakage and conflict risks when paired with a prompt-leakage agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a reads and writes files and processes stdin/stdout, so if agent_b’s outputs are copied into shared files or streams, prompt-like content can be ingested. agent_b is a prompt-leakage corpus, so the pair creates a plausible injection bridge, though no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs are copied into files that agent_a reads
IF the two agents share stdin/stdout or a shared workspace
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic file ingestion for agent_a
Require human review before copying agent_b outputs into agent_a
Use content tagging to mark untrusted text
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches secrets and many file-backed data classes, and can send data to allowlisted external APIs; agent_b has no egress, so the main leakage path is from agent_a rather than a bidirectional channel. The pair still risks sensitive data exposure if shared files or copied outputs move into agent_a’s outbound requests.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in agent_a’s workspace
IF agent_a forwards file contents to an allowlisted API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Restrict agent_a to non-sensitive datasets
Review outbound requests before execution
Rotate any exposed tokens immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while agent_b’s profile exposes no write surface, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. However, if both are run against the same workspace, agent_a can overwrite artifacts that agent_b depends on, making coordination failures plausible even without modify_git_state on either side.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory
IF agent_b consumes artifacts produced by agent_a
mitigations: Use per-agent directories
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Make outputs immutable after generation
Snapshot work before agent_a writes
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate files, logs, and training outputs that agent_b may treat as authoritative if copied into its workflow. Because agent_b is a prompt-leakage-oriented corpus with no verification surface documented, the pair can propagate mistaken or malicious content unless an explicit review step is inserted.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-produced files as source material
IF no verification step checks agent_a outputs before reuse
mitigations: Require manual verification of agent_a outputs
Label generated artifacts as untrusted
Keep agent_b from auto-consuming agent_a files
Use checksum-based handoff for artifacts
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles hub_token and sdk-token secrets and may contact third-party APIs, while agent_b has no documented data classes or egress. The compliance risk is mainly on agent_a’s side; no residency or certification mismatch is documented for agent_b, so this is a limited, one-sided concern rather than a pairwise breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_a’s API calls
IF retention or residency rules apply to those secrets
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in agent_a workflows
Confirm API destinations before use
Minimize token scope
Purge logs after runs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
